title: [RFC]: A registry + CI ratchet so tuned Triton kernel configs cannot silently rot
author: access2rohit
body:
**TL;DR:** vLLM's block-INT8 tuned-config loader silently matched **0 of 39** shipped config files for ~14 months -- a one-character filename typo (`block_shape=[128, 128]` vs the shipped `[128,128]`) meant every block-INT8 model quietly fell back to the heuristic, with no test, warning, or signal. The fix shipped; this RFC proposes a small registry + a CI check so that **class** of bug cannot silently recur for any tuned Triton kernel -- without forcing anyone to tune a kernel that should not be tuned.

_(Reference implementation -- registry, decorator, AST kernel discovery, reasoned allowlist, ratchet, tests -- is built and green. Branch: https://github.com/access2rohit/vllm/tree/rfc/tunable-kernels-A3-B3 .)_

## Motivation

vLLM ships offline-tuned Triton kernel configs (JSON keyed by batch size M) for a handful of
compute-heavy, on-the-hot-path kernels -- MoE expert GEMMs, block-FP8/INT8 GEMMs, the Mamba
selective_state_update decode step -- and loads the best match at runtime, falling back to a fixed
heuristic on a miss. This is high-value: the right tile/num_warps/num_stages for a shape+GPU is a
real speedup, and the env override (VLLM_TUNED_CONFIG_FOLDER) lets operators hot-load new configs
without rebuilding.

Two structural gaps make this fragile:

1. No uniform "make a kernel tunable" mechanism. Each of the 4 tunable kernels hand-rolls its own
   config-file lookup (its own filename f-string + its own load + fallback). There is no shared
   contract and no programmatic list of which kernels are tunable. A newly added compute-heavy
   kernel easily ships with no tuning path at all, and nobody notices.

2. Silent drift, with a concrete 14-month precedent. The block-INT8 loader built its filename with a
   stray space -- `block_shape=[128, 128]` -- while every shipped INT8 config is `[128,128]`. Result:
   0 of 39 configs ever matched; the loader silently fell back to the heuristic from #16366
   (2025-04) until it was found and fixed in the recent hot-load work. No test, no warning, no
   signal -- just quietly lost performance on every block-INT8 model for over a year.

The root cause of both: "is this kernel tunable, and does its loader actually work?" is answered
ad hoc per kernel, with nothing enforcing consistency. We propose a small, idiomatic mechanism +
an opt-out CI check that makes the answer explicit and regression-proof -- without forcing anyone
to tune a kernel that should not be tuned.

Non-goal: deciding which kernels are compute-heavy/in-path. No static check can infer that; the
proposal makes that human judgment explicit and reviewable, not automated.

## Proposed Change

Two pieces -- a registry (mechanism) and a completeness ratchet with a reasoned allowlist (enforcement):

### Part 1 -- A registry of tunable kernels (mechanism)

A single importable source of truth, mirroring vLLM's existing model / attention-backend
registries:

- `vllm/utils/tuned_config_registry.py`: a frozen `TunableKernelSpec(name, applicability, key_fn,
  packaged_dir)`, a `TUNABLE_KERNEL_REGISTRY` dict, `register_tunable_kernel`, `get_tunable_kernels`,
  and a generic resolve+select front-end `get_tuned_config_for(name, M, **shape)` that returns the
  single nearest-M config (or None). `applicability` is an enum
  (COMPUTE_HEAVY_INPATH / OPTIONAL / EXPERIMENTAL).
- A `tunable_triton_kernel(...)` decorator (optional ergonomic front-end) that wraps a kernel's
  config getter to do filename-build + load + fallback AND register the spec at import time.
- The 4 existing tunable kernels are registered by a seed module whose key_fns reproduce each
  loader's exact filename (so the registry's view matches what each kernel actually searches for).

Adoption cost is small and is NOT new: all 4 tunable kernels already have a per-kernel config getter
today; this standardizes them and centralizes the lookup logic that was being copy-pasted (the
copy-paste is exactly what produced the INT8 space bug). Making a kernel tunable does NOT touch the
`@triton.jit` body; the irreducible per-kernel work is a ~3-line filename builder + wiring the
launch site to use the loaded config (intrinsic to "use a tuned value instead of a hardcoded one").

### Part 2 -- A completeness ratchet with a reasoned allowlist (enforcement)

A CI test (`tests/test_tunable_kernels_ratchet.py`) that:

- Enumerates every `@triton.jit` kernel via a static AST walk (`tools/tuned_config/discover_kernels.py`)
  -- no imports, so it is robust to torch/CUDA/platform-gated modules and sees every kernel.
- Requires each discovered kernel to be EITHER registered tunable OR listed in
  `tools/tuned_config/exempt_kernels.py` with a one-line reason.
- Is seeded once with all current kernels (the ratchet baseline), so it is GREEN today and only
  bites a NEWLY added kernel. A new kernel makes CI fail with an actionable message:
  "New @triton.jit kernel(s) [...] must either register a tuned-config loader OR be added to
  exempt_kernels.py with a reason (e.g. 'memory-bound elementwise; tuning <2%')."
- Also runs a generic filename round-trip check on every registered kernel (asserts the key_fn
  output is exactly what the loader searches for) -- this single test structurally prevents the
  INT8-class bug for all current and future tunable kernels at once.
- Rejects empty / "TODO" exemption reasons, so the allowlist cannot become a rubber stamp.

The reasoned allowlist is deliberately the de-coercion mechanism. CI never says "you must tune this
kernel" -- only "tune it OR state, in one reviewed line, why not." That keeps the ~88% of kernels
that are memory-bound (rmsnorm, rope, activation, ...) out of scope by an explicit, reviewed
decision rather than silent omission. The allowlist is what keeps the check from being a blunt
mandate: without it, the test would flag 324 of 328 kernels on the current tree -- almost all
memory-bound kernels that should never be tuned.

### Why both, together

The registry without the ratchet (Part 1 only) catches filename drift on kernels people remember to
register, but a forgotten kernel stays forgotten. The ratchet needs the registry's machine-readable
list to know what is covered. Together they make "tunable or explicitly-not" a property CI
guarantees. The registry doubles as living documentation of every perf-critical kernel and the
tuning status of every other one.

### Rollout / scope

- The 4 existing tunable kernels are migrated onto the registry (behavior-preserving; their current
  tests stay green).
- The allowlist is seeded with all currently-discovered non-tunable kernels, each with a reason
  (specific for known memory-bound kernels, generic otherwise) -- a one-time mechanical step so CI
  starts green.
- No kernel is forced to change. Existing config files and the VLLM_TUNED_CONFIG_FOLDER override are
  untouched.
- A reference implementation (registry + decorator + seed + discovery + allowlist + ratchet + tests)
  is built and passing; happy to open it as a draft PR for review.

## Feedback Period

Two weeks (suggested). Main discussion points we expect:
- The small per-new-kernel contributor friction (register OR exempt-with-reason) vs. the
  silent-drift risk it removes.
- Whether "compute-heavy and in-path" warrants a written definition (FLOPs/byte? on the decode
  path?) to guide allowlist review, or stays reviewer judgment.
- Whether `applicability=COMPUTE_HEAVY_INPATH` should be enforced (must be tunable) or advisory.
- Landing as one PR (registry + ratchet) or two (mechanism first, enforcement second).

## Any Other Things

- This is additive and low-risk: default behavior (env var unset) is unchanged; the ratchet starts
  green; the round-trip test only fails on genuine filename drift.
- The mechanism is forward-compatible with a future tuning service: the registry is exactly the
  machine-readable manifest of "what is tunable, with what key, and how to regenerate it."
- A natural follow-up (separate PR) is bringing additional compute-heavy kernels into the registry --
  e.g. the unified Triton attention kernel, which today selects its tile from a fixed heuristic.

title: [RFC]: Kernel-agnostic constant-stride (layer-major) KV cache layout for KV connectors
author: xiaguan
body:
## Motivation

#27743 added "cross-layer KV blocks" so a KV connector can stage/transfer a block's KV for
all layers at once, by allocating all layers in one tensor (`use_uniform_kv_cache` /
`allocate_uniform_kv_caches`).

For MLA backends the only supported physical layout was **block-major**
`(num_blocks, num_layers, ...)`. That makes each per-layer view a *strided* (non-contiguous)
slice, and MLA kernels require contiguous per-layer views — so #37090 **disabled cross-layer
KV for all MLA backends** (`get_kv_cache_stride_order(include_num_layers_dimension=True)`
returns the identity permutation to signal "unsupported").

The result: the cross-layer connector optimization is off for exactly the models that dominate
disaggregated prefill/decode and KV offloading today — DeepSeek V3/V3.2, GLM, Kimi, all MLA.
With it disabled, vLLM falls back to **one independent `torch.zeros` per layer**, so a connector
sees `L` allocations at unrelated base addresses. Two concrete costs:

1. The GPU↔staging layer↔page transpose needs `L` separate copies per block — there is no
   constant stride across layers to exploit.
2. RDMA connectors must register `L` memory regions (one per layer) instead of one.

## Proposed Change

Add a **second uniform layout: layer-major contiguous slices**. Allocate one buffer for all
same-spec layers and hand each layer a **contiguous slice** at a constant stride
`S = num_blocks * page_size_bytes`. The per-layer view stays contiguous and bit-identical to a
standalone tensor, so **attention kernels (including MLA) are unaffected** — no
`get_kv_cache_stride_order` support is required. This is kernel-agnostic, unlike the existing
block-major path.

```
Today — one independent torch.zeros per layer (cross-layer disabled for MLA, #37090):

  layer 0   : [ blk0 blk1 ... blkN ]   @ ptr0
  layer 1   : [ blk0 blk1 ... blkN ]   @ ptr1     (ptr1 - ptr0 : arbitrary)
   ...
  layer L-1 : [ blk0 blk1 ... blkN ]   @ ptr(L-1) (no constant stride)

  => L memory regions; gathering block b across layers = L copies at L unrelated addresses


Proposed — one buffer, per-layer CONTIGUOUS slices, constant stride S = num_blocks * page_size_bytes:

  base -> +--------- layer 0 ---------+--------- layer 1 ---------+ ... +-------- layer L-1 -------+
          | blk0 blk1 ...      blkN   | blk0 blk1 ...      blkN   |     | blk0 blk1 ...      blkN  |
          +--------------------------+--------------------------+     +-------------------------+
          ^                          ^                          ^
          base + 0*S                 base + 1*S                 base + (L-1)*S

  per-layer view  = base + l*S            (contiguous slice, identical to standalone -> kernel safe)
  block b, layers = base + l*S + b*blk    for l in [0, L)   => CONSTANT inter-layer stride S
```

Two concrete wins for connectors, both from the constant stride / single allocation:

**1. `cudaMemcpy2D` transpose (zero SM).** Gather a block across all layers into a contiguous
page in one copy-engine 2D op, instead of `L` separate copies:

```
cudaMemcpy2D(dst    = page_b,                 // contiguous staging page, L * blk bytes
             dpitch = blk,
             src    = base + b*blk,           // block b of layer 0
             spitch = S,                      // constant inter-layer stride
             width  = blk,
             height = L)
// runs on the copy engine (0 SM), one launch per block; today: L memcpys per block
```

**2. Single memory registration.** One allocation → connectors register **one** RDMA memory
region (one rkey) / one CUDA IPC handle for all layers, instead of `L`.

Implementation sketch:
- `_allocate_kv_cache_tensors`: one `torch.zeros(total)` sliced per page-size bucket, instead of
  N independent `torch.zeros`. Downstream `_reshape_kv_cache_tensors` is unchanged — contiguous
  int8 slices support `.view(dtype)` / `as_strided`, and `storage_offset` is carried (vLLM core
  already tolerates non-zero kv-cache `storage_offset`: Mamba state tensors and Triton fp8 scales
  use `as_strided` with offsets today).
- Gate behind a new connector preference, weaker than `prefer_cross_layer_blocks` (which signals
  the block-major layout): a connector opts in when it only needs a constant inter-layer stride,
  not per-block contiguity.

Open API questions for discussion:
- How to advertise/select this layout — a new connector preference, or a backend-level capability
  flag distinct from the existing block-major `stride_order[0] != 0` signal?
- How to communicate the inter-layer stride to the connector — explicit (registration field /
  callback) vs. the connector detecting that per-layer `data_ptr`s are arithmetic.

This is purely additive and opt-in; default allocation is unchanged.

## Feedback Period

1–2 weeks.

## CC List

Builds on #27743 (cross-layer KV blocks) and #37090 (cross-layer disabled for MLA).

## Any Other Things

We maintain [PegaFlow](https://github.com/novitalabs/pegaflow), a disaggregated KV connector
(RDMA across nodes + tiered host/SSD storage). We are moving its CPU-side KV from layer-first to
**page-first** (a block's all-layer KV contiguous on the host) to cut per-block metadata by a
factor of `num_layers` — one RDMA descriptor / one SSD iovec / one storage slot per block instead
of one per (layer). The transpose from vLLM's per-layer GPU layout into that page is the operation
this RFC makes cheap: with a constant inter-layer stride it is one `cudaMemcpy2D` per block on the
copy engine. We are happy to contribute the vLLM-side allocation change and a unit test mirroring
`tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_kv_cache_layout.py`.

title: [RFC]: Heterogeneous TP<->DP parallelism across the P/D disaggregation boundary (MoRIIO)
author: edwinlim0919
body:
<!--
RFC issue  —  template: .github/ISSUE_TEMPLATE/750-RFC.yml
Title: [RFC]: Heterogeneous TP<->DP parallelism across the P/D disaggregation boundary (MoRIIO)
Implementation PRs (all standalone on main): #46116 routing, #46115 proxy fix, #47495 backpressure.
Labels: RFC. CC the MoRIIO/KV-connector + ROCm reviewers (from #29304).
-->

# [RFC]: Heterogeneous TP↔DP parallelism across the P/D disaggregation boundary (MoRIIO)

## Motivation

Disaggregated prefill/decode lets the two phases run with **different** optimal parallelism, but MoRIIO today assumes the prefill and decode engines share the same parallelism layout (DP8EP↔DP8EP, or TP8↔TP8).

The two phases can benefit from different parallelism configurations. For example, on an 8K-in/1K-out DeepSeek-R1 workload (run on MI300X / gfx942):

- **Prefill** is latency-bound → **TP** wins TTFT (TP8 ≈ 1s vs DP8EP ≈ 10s).
- **Decode** is throughput-bound at higher concurrency → **DP/EP** scales (DP8EP keeps scaling ≥ c256).

So at high concurrencies, the best deployment option could be **heterogeneous**. With prefill nodes configured in TP8 mode and decode nodes configured in DP8EP mode, we can achieve low TTFT from the TP8 prefill, and scalable throughput at high request loads (e.g. 512 concurrent request load).

The performance results below show the benefit of the heterogeneous setup. Various concurrency levels were tested, which control the maximum number of requests that are allowed to being served at once in the P/D setup. For each concurrency level, 10 * C total requests were sent, where C is the concurrency. Warmups were also done to prevent cold start from affecting the reported performance.

At the highest concurrency tested (512 concurrency requests), the mixed parallelism 2P_TP8:1D_DP8EP setup achieves the highest throughput and lowest TTFT of the three configurations.


### Config 1: 2P_TP8 : 1D_TP8 (homogeneous TP8)
| Concurrency | Total throughput (tok/s) | Generation throughput (tok/s) | Mean TPOT (ms) | Mean TTFT (ms) | Benchmark duration (s) |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| c32 | 8,603 | 961 | 30.3 | 1,270 | 307.8 |
| c128 | 27,576 | 3,051 | 37.6 | 2,497 | 385.6 |
| c512 | 38,407 | 4,263 | 55.9 | 55,179 | 1,106.2 |

### Config 2: 2P_DP8EP : 1D_DP8EP (homogeneous DP8EP)
| Concurrency | Total throughput (tok/s) | Generation throughput (tok/s) | Mean TPOT (ms) | Mean TTFT (ms) | Benchmark duration (s) |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| c32 | 6,893 | 770 | 34.9 | 4,448 | 384.2 |
| c128 | 22,749 | 2,517 | 37.9 | 10,123 | 467.4 |
| c512 | 34,935 | 3,878 | 42.3 | 77,155 | 1,216.1 |

### Config 3: 2P_TP8 : 1D_DP8EP (MIXED)
| Concurrency | Total throughput (tok/s) | Generation throughput (tok/s) | Mean TPOT (ms) | Mean TTFT (ms) | Benchmark duration (s) |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| c32 | 7,291 | 814 | 36.2 | 1,362 | 363.2 |
| c128 | 21,760 | 2,408 | 48.7 | 2,535 | 488.6 |
| c512 | **42,349** | **4,701** | 55.0 | **46,052** | **1,003.2** |


One target topologies has been enabled and validated by the PRs in this RFC:
- **Forward**: `P_DP8EP → D_TP8` (DP/EP prefill, TP decode). This is the configuration described above.

TODO in future work: We did not do extensive validation on the mirror version, since this configuration doesnt have good performance characteristics in our evaluations. Future work can validate it, but it is considered out of scope of this RFC.
- **Mirror** : `P_TP8  → D_DP8EP` (TP prefill, DP/EP decode). The mirror of the configuration described above.

## Proposed Change

The P/D KV transfer must route reads across engines whose `(dp_size, tp_size)` differ. Design (describing behaviour, not the diff):

1. **Source-rank resolution lives in the connector, not the proxy.**
The proxy only does coarse instance + DP-rank request distribution; the *KV source rank* is a connector decision because only the connector knows the KV layout (MLA-replicated vs partitioned).

2. **Per-`(dp, tp)` session keying.**
Sessions/handshake state are keyed by `(engine, dp_rank, tp_rank)` (`get_engine_name_with_dp_tp`) so each remote prefill rank gets its own session + memory-region metadata, instead of a single DP-only key.

3. **Flexible prefill-TP read (this RFC's headline mechanism).**
For a TP-replicated prefill (prefill TP + MLA) feeding a TP1 decode, the latent KV is replicated across all prefill TP ranks, so *any* rank is a valid source. Previously, heterogeneous parallelism PD setups would only read from a single TP rank (TP0), rather than distributing READ load across multiple ranks. The connector picks a prefill TP rank per read via deterministic round-robin to spread reads and prefill NIC load across TP0...N-1. Gated on: `world_size==1` (decode TP1 → no local TP collective to keep in lockstep over the choice), `use_mla` (KV replicated), and `remote_dp_size==1 && remote_tp_size>1` (a pure-TP prefill with >1 rank). Outside the gate the source rank stays fixed by the local-rank mapping. This is byte-identical to current behaviour.
**Future work:**
The gate currently requires a *pure-TP* prefill (`remote_dp_size == 1`). An intra-node DP×TP prefill (e.g. `DP4TP2`) falls back to the fixed-rank read; extending the random spread to "a random TP rank *within* the request's DP partition" is a localized follow-up (the `(dp, tp)` threading is already in place).

4. **Consistent rank threading.** The chosen rank flows through the session key, the build-on-demand handshake, the peer-host resolution and the read-completion notify port, so a read and its completion notify always address the same prefill rank (a drift leaks the prefill buffer → MR overflow).

### Implementation PRs
The implementation is split into focused, **independent** PRs, all standalone on
`main` (no cross-dependencies):
- **#46116** `[Core][KV-transfer]`: heterogeneous TP<->DP read routing: DP-rank read routing, per-`(dp, tp)` session keying, the flexible prefill-TP read (§3), and an eager pre-forward handshake so mixed configs don't deadlock.
- **#46115** `[Bugfix]`: toy-proxy DP-rank index-aliasing fix (the §1 request distribution layer) + high-concurrency proxy hardening.
- **#47495** `[Bugfix]`: RDMA send-queue full backpressure retry: general MoRIIO READ robustness needed at high concurrency.

(Earlier drafts of #46116 stacked on the in-flight wideTP PRs #45228/#45230; it has since been rebuilt to stand alone on `main` and no longer depends on them.)

## Feedback Period
≥ 1 week.

## CC List
@inkcherry (MoRIIO connector author, #29304) @KuntaiDu @DarkLight1337 (KV-transfer / core) @gshtras @tjtanaa (ROCm) @chaeminlim-mb (MoRIIO / heterogeneous-PD).

## Any Other Things
- This is ROCm/MoRIIO-specific (gfx942, AITER MLA).

## Related work (implementation PRs)
- **#46116** `[Core][KV-transfer]` heterogeneous TP<->DP read routing: the §2-§4 mechanism. Standalone on `main`.
- **#46115** `[Bugfix]` proxy DP-rank index-aliasing fix: the §1 distribution layer.
- **#47495** `[Bugfix]` RDMA send-queue-full backpressure retry: READ robustness.

## Before submitting
- [x] Searched existing issues/RFCs for heterogeneous-PD / mixed-parallelism no existing RFC for heterogeneous TP↔DP MoRIIO parallelism; closest prior art is the NIXL block-*size* work (#42895, RFC #26744, PR #30275), a different axis.
- [x] Asked the docs chatbot.

title: [RFC]: Support for Domino speculative decoding in vLLM
author: GIREESH7963
body:
# [RFC]: Support for Domino speculative decoding in vLLM

> **Provenance.** Technical claims below are grounded in: the Domino paper
> (arXiv 2605.29707v1); the public `Huang2020/Qwen3-8B-Domino-b16` checkpoint
> (its `config.json` and the full `model.safetensors` tensor manifest, read
> directly); and a read of vLLM `main`'s `vllm/v1/spec_decode/` verified at
> commit `2396d91` (2026-06-25). The subsystem refactors often — re-confirm the
> vLLM line references against current main before relying on them.

## Motivation

vLLM supports a family of model-based speculative-decoding methods (EAGLE /
EAGLE-3, MTP, PARD, DFlash, draft-model). **Domino is not currently available
in vLLM.** Public Domino draft checkpoints exist (e.g.
`Huang2020/Qwen3-8B-Domino-b16`) and the authors provide a reference
implementation, but it is, per the paper, "mainly adapted to SGLang" — there is
no path to serve Domino under vLLM today.

The core idea (Domino, Huang et al., arXiv 2605.29707): speculative decoding is
bottlenecked by a quality–cost tradeoff. Autoregressive drafters (EAGLE) model
causal dependencies between draft tokens but pay a sequential per-token cost;
parallel drafters (DFlash) draft a whole block in one forward pass but lose
intra-block causal structure. Domino keeps drafting parallel — a parallel
backbone produces preliminary block logits in one pass — then applies a
lightweight **Domino head** that injects causal information as a low-rank
**residual correction in logit space**, avoiding any repeated draft-model or
full-LM-head execution.

**Why it's worth adding (authors' results, on A100 — not yet reproduced under
vLLM):**
- Up to 5.49× end-to-end speedup (Transformers backend) and up to ~5.8×
  throughput (SGLang) on Qwen3.
- vs. DFlash specifically: +56M params (+5.3%), only +2.8% draft-then-verify
  latency, but +16.6% average acceptance length and +12.3% end-to-end speedup.
- Head ablation (same model, correction off→on): avg acceptance length
  3.49 → 4.19, avg speedup 2.84× → 3.31×.

These are the authors' numbers under their stack. Establishing what holds under
vLLM is precisely the goal of this work (see Benchmarking).

## Key framing: Domino is a head on top of DFlash, which vLLM already has

This is the crux of why the integration is tractable. The published Domino
backbone **is** the DFlash architecture (Chen et al., arXiv 2602.06036), and
vLLM already ships a `DFlashProposer` (`vllm/v1/spec_decode/dflash.py`). The
public checkpoint confirms this directly: its `architectures` is
`["DFlashDraftModel"]` and the Domino head is declared as
`dflash_config.projector_type = "domino"` — i.e. the checkpoint is a DFlash
draft model *plus* a Domino projector, not a new architecture.

So this RFC does **not** propose a drafter from scratch. It proposes adding the
~56M-parameter Domino correction head (a GRU + a low-rank MLP) on top of vLLM's
existing DFlash proposer path.

## Where this fits in vLLM (proposed design)

vLLM V1 spec-decode is a proposer/verifier architecture. The verifier (target
model + rejection sampler) is method-agnostic and is **not** modified here. All
method-specific logic lives in a proposer subclass of `SpecDecodeBaseProposer`
(`vllm/v1/spec_decode/llm_base_proposer.py`, class at line 62 as of `2396d91`).
`DFlashProposer` is such a subclass today.

Domino is structurally **a sequential correction on a parallel drafter**:
- DFlash is a *parallel* drafter — it drafts all K block positions in one
  forward pass.
- The base `propose()` takes a single-pass early-return when `parallel_drafting`
  is set (`if self.num_speculative_tokens == 1 or self.parallel_drafting:` in
  `llm_base_proposer.py`; the later `only_one_forward_pass = is_graph_capturing
  or self.parallel_drafting` path uses the same flag). So a parallel drafter
  makes exactly **one** draft-sampling call holding all K positions' base logits
  at once.
- Domino's correction is in *logit space* on those base logits (the paper is
  explicit: hidden-space correction would force re-running the full LM head per
  step). This is what makes a single sampling override the natural home for it.

### Proposed implementation: `DominoProposer` (mirrors `DFlashProposer`)

1. **`__init__`** — assert `method == "domino"`; `super().__init__(...,
   pass_hidden_states_to_model=True)` (the same flag `DFlashProposer` passes);
   read `pure_draft_prefix_len` (=1 in the public ckpt) and `gru_hidden_dim`
   (=1024) from `dflash_config`; expect `prefix_gru` / `embed_proj` on the draft
   model.
2. **`set_inputs_first_pass`** — call `super()` to inherit DFlash's
   cross-attention input layout unchanged, then stash the bonus tokens
   (`next_token_ids`). Target hidden states (`z`/`H_i`) are already stashed by
   the DFlash parent as `self._dflash_hidden_states` (`dflash.py`,
   `set_inputs_first_pass`). This is the same stash-on-self pattern DFlash
   already uses.
3. **Sampling override (the Domino head).** Because of the parallel single-pass
   layout, the sampling step receives all K positions' logits at once. Per the
   `_sample_from_logits` contract in `llm_base_proposer.py`, parallel drafters
   pass `batch_size * K` rows, **request-major** (K consecutive slots per
   request). Reshape to `[N, K, V]` and run the correction loop, which is a
   near-direct port of the reference's legacy path:
     - positions `< pure_draft_prefix_len`: argmax base logits, no correction.
     - prime the GRU on `[bonus, prefix_drafts]` embeddings.
     - for `i in range(prefix_len, K)`:
         `Δ_i = embed_proj(cat([H_i, S_{i-1}]))`; `logits_i = base_i + Δ_i`;
         `tok_i = argmax(logits_i)`; embed `tok_i`; advance GRU to `S_i`.
     - apply a draft→target token remap (`d2t`) only if the config defines one.
       The public `b16` checkpoint does **not** — its head emits full target
       vocab (see below), so no remap applies.

   **Design choice — see Alternatives.** The GRU state must thread across the K
   positions; the question is *where* that loop lives.

### New draft-model class: `DominoForCausalLM` (or extend the DFlash model class)

Carries the Domino head and loads its weights. **Verified against the public
`Qwen3-8B-Domino-b16` checkpoint** — keys and shapes read directly from the
`model.safetensors` manifest (62 tensors total):

| weight key | shape | role |
|---|---|---|
| `prefix_gru.weight_ih_l0` | `[3072, 4096]` | GRU input→gates; in=hidden_size 4096, 3072 = 3×1024 (r/z/n gates) |
| `prefix_gru.weight_hh_l0` | `[3072, 1024]` | GRU hidden→gates; gru_hidden_dim 1024 |
| `embed_proj.0.weight` | `[256, 5120]` | W1; in = **5120 = 4096 + 1024** = [H_i ; S_{i-1}] concat |
| `embed_proj.2.weight` | `[151936, 256]` | W2; low-rank r=256 → **full vocab** 151936 |

Notes that matter for the loader (all confirmed against the full manifest):
- **The entire head is bias-free.** The full state dict contains **no `bias`
  tensors anywhere** — neither GRU (`bias_ih_l0`/`bias_hh_l0` absent) nor the
  `embed_proj` Linears. Construct as `nn.GRU(4096, 1024, bias=False)` and both
  `embed_proj` Linears as `bias=False`, or weight-loading will look for bias
  tensors that don't exist.
- `embed_proj` is `Linear(5120→256, bias=False) → SiLU → Linear(256→151936,
  bias=False)`; the index `.0` / `.2` is an `nn.Sequential` with SiLU at `.1`.
- The correction emits a **full-vocab** logit bias, added to base logits before
  argmax — not a reduced-vocab correction. There is no `d2t`/`t2d` tensor in the
  checkpoint, consistent with `vocab_size == 151936` end to end.
- Backbone pieces (`fc.weight [4096, 20480]` = projection over the 5 captured
  target layers, 5×4096; `hidden_norm`, the 5 transformer `layers.{0..4}`,
  `norm`) are **inherited DFlash machinery**, already handled by `DFlashProposer`
  — not part of the Domino delta. They reinforce the "head on existing backbone"
  framing.

### Config / registration contract

From the public checkpoint's `config.json` (all values read directly):
- `architectures: ["DFlashDraftModel"]`, `model_type: "qwen3"`,
  `auto_map.AutoModel: "dflash.DFlashDraftModel"` (the HF path expects DFlash's
  custom modeling file — vLLM-native support is the actual work, vs.
  trust-remote-code).
- `dflash_config`: `projector_type="domino"`, `gru_hidden_dim=1024`,
  `emb_dim`/r `=256`, `pure_draft_prefix_len=1`, `mask_token_id=151669`,
  `shift_label=true`, `target_layer_ids=[1,9,17,25,33]`.
- Top level: `block_size=16`, `num_hidden_layers=5`, `hidden_size=4096`,
  `vocab_size=151936`.

Proposed: register `method="domino"` routing to `DominoProposer`; the draft
config must set `parallel_drafting` and carry `mask_token_id` **inside
`dflash_config`** — vLLM's `_init_parallel_drafting_params` reads
`dflash_config["mask_token_id"]` for this code path and raises if it is absent
(`llm_base_proposer.py`, lines ~331–349 at `2396d91`).

## Alternatives considered

**Alternative A — override the K-step loop in `propose()` to thread GRU state.**
Faithful to the reference (which owns its whole loop), but duplicates a large
part of the base class's biggest method and increases drift surface against
future spec-decode refactors.

**Proposed (B) — keep DFlash's single-pass layout; run the sequential GRU
correction inside an overridden sampling step.** Smaller, more stable override
surface; matches both the reference's "produce all K tokens in one call" shape
and the paper's logit-space design. The GRU is still walked sequentially over
the K rows, but *inside* that one sampling call. The control-flow precondition
(a single sampling call for parallel drafters) holds on current main — see the
`parallel_drafting` early-return above.

I propose **B**. One genuinely open design question for the team: should
`DominoProposer` subclass `DFlashProposer` directly, share a new intermediate
base, or stand alone? That depends on where the spec-decode subsystem is headed,
so I'd rather have maintainers' read than presume. (See Open Questions.)

## Proposed plan / phases (discrete reviewed PRs, not one drop)

1. `DominoForCausalLM` draft model + weight loading (the 4 head tensors above,
   all `bias=False`), reusing the DFlash backbone loader.
2. `DominoProposer` + `method="domino"` registration.
3. Correctness: token-parity vs the reference's **legacy** (cuDNN-GRU +
   nn.Sequential, cat-then-Linear) path. Methodology: greedy decoding, fixed
   seed, identical prompts, compare argmax token IDs per block position between
   vLLM `DominoProposer` and the reference. Target is exact per-position token
   parity on the draft block; the acceptance-length/speedup numbers are reported
   separately under Benchmarking and left blank until measured.
4. Benchmarking + docs.

**Benchmarking caveat (state plainly):** the paper's speedups are on A100 under
SGLang/Transformers; the reference is "mainly adapted to SGLang." Initial vLLM
validation here is on a T4 and is correctness-oriented — T4 perf is **not**
representative of Domino's intended hardware, and the efficiency-engineering the
authors use (fused Triton kernels, CUDA Graphs) is out of scope for v1. Do not
claim the paper's speedups will reproduce under vLLM; measuring that is the goal.

## Open questions

- **Subclassing (above):** `DominoProposer` subclasses `DFlashProposer`, a new
  shared base, or stands alone?
- **Head-offset special-casing.** In `llm_base_proposer.py` the per-request head
  offset is computed as
  `1 if (pass_hidden_states_to_model and self.method != "dflash") else 0`.
  DFlash is explicitly special-cased to `0`; a new `method="domino"` would take
  the `!= "dflash"` branch and get `1`. Whether Domino should join DFlash's
  special case (or whether the offset is correct as-is for it) needs a
  maintainer's eye — it affects input layout, not just registration.
- **Draft-config schema** vLLM expects for a *new* parallel-drafting method
  beyond `mask_token_id` (e.g. how `block_size`/`num_speculative_tokens` are
  surfaced for Domino).
- **Tree vs block:** Domino/DFlash are block-parallel (no draft tree); confirm
  the proposer stays on vLLM's block verification path, not tree decoding.

*Resolved during drafting (recorded so reviewers don't re-ask): the `embed_proj`
Linears carry no bias (whole head is bias-free), and this checkpoint has no
`d2t` remap (full-vocab head). Both verified against the `model.safetensors`
manifest.*

title: [RFC]: Extension points for backends whose physical layout isn't a permutation of the logical layout (weights, quant scales, KV-cache, MLA, EP)
author: ChuanLi1101
body:
# [RFC]: Extension points for backends whose physical layout isn't a permutation of the logical layout (weights, quant scales, KV-cache, MLA, EP)

> AI assistance was used to draft this RFC; a human submitter has reviewed and defends every claim. Code evidence is staged at ROCm/aiter#3885.

### Motivation.

vLLM already has three in-flight efforts that move layout handling in exactly the right direction, and we want to build on them rather than duplicate them:

- **#42082 (Standardize KV-cache Layouts)** — a standard logical KV shape `[L, B, H, N, <content>]` with physical layout selected by a `stride_order` permutation; KV-connectors become backend-agnostic.
- **#8913 (QuantizationConfig / QuantizeMethodBase Refactor)** — decouple checkpoint format from kernel, describe the computation so a dispatcher can pick a kernel that `can_implement` it.
- **#33314 (Apply #8913 to Quantized Linear Methods)** — a canonical `LinearParams` representation plus a per-kernel `process_weights_after_loading` repack/reorder hook.

We've been integrating AMD AITER kernels (CK / ASM / Triton) under vLLM and find these three already cover most of what we need for **linear weights and quant scales**, and the *permutation-expressible* part of KV layout. This RFC is **not** a competing design; it asks whether a handful of remaining extension points — needed by any backend whose physical layout is **not** a permutation/repack of the default — can be folded into those efforts.

Concretely, today the only way to run AITER under vLLM is a translation shim that reshapes/shuffles weights at load and re-`view()`/`permute()`s tensors on every forward pass. The shim is fragile, costs memory/latency, and re-implements logic vLLM owns (TP sharding, accounting, block management). AITER is just our concrete case; the gaps below are general to any backend with a genuinely different native layout.

### Proposed Change.

For each gap we note the existing RFC it extends and why that RFC, as currently scoped, doesn't yet express it.

**1. KV layouts beyond a stride permutation (extends #42082).**
#42082's `stride_order` expresses physical layout as a *permutation* of `[L, B, H, N, C]`. Some decode kernels need layouts that are not permutations of the logical dims:
- a head dim factorized into `[dim/x, x]` micro-tiles (a reshape, not a permutation);
- **K and V using different layouts** (e.g. K rank-5, V rank-4) rather than a symmetric `[2, head_dim]` content;
- **scheduler block size ≠ kernel block size** (kernel supports only a fixed set, e.g. `{256, 1024}`), requiring a virtual↔physical block-table translation.
Ask: let a backend declare a physical KV layout richer than a permutation, and let the framework own the virtual↔physical block-table mapping (so it isn't re-implemented per backend). Since #42082 / PR #42374 plan to remove `get_kv_cache_stride_order` and `get_kv_cache_shape`, it would be good to land this extension in the same redesign rather than after.

**2. MoE weight/scale repacking (extends #33314).**
#33314's canonical representation + per-kernel preprocessing hook is exactly what we want for linear weights (our 16×16 "bpreshuffle" would be a kernel preprocessing step). But it explicitly scopes out FusedMoE, and the bulk of AITER's weight/scale repacking is in MoE (pre-shuffled expert weights, two incompatible layouts depending on the kernel path). Ask: a parallel (not necessarily shared) repack hook for MoE expert weights, or confirmation of where MoE layout repacking is meant to live.

**3. Additional quant-scale axes (extends #8913 / #33314).**
The canonical scale types (per-tensor / channel / block / group) don't yet capture axes some kernels require:
- **scale orientation** (row- vs column-major, kernel-dependent);
- **scale dtype** beyond fp32, incl. UE8M0 / uint8 microscaling;
- **FP8 variant** (`e4m3fn` vs `e4m3fnuz`).
Ask: include these as declarable axes in the descriptor so they don't have to be hand-managed downstream.

**4. Alignment / padding as a declared property (new).**
Several kernels impose hard divisibility (pad hidden/intermediate, pad rows to a multiple of 16/32, MLA ≥16 heads). Today a backend pads into larger buffers and slices back, carrying pad-slack metadata, because TP sharding / KV & weight accounting assume exact model dims. Ask: let a backend declare "physical padded shape ≠ logical shape" so sharding/accounting/loading handle it without per-model glue.

**5. MLA paging extensions (extends #42082).**
#42082 can express the MLA latent as `state_content`, but not: `page_size = 1` token-linear indexing, auxiliary per-layer caches (e.g. a sparse FP8 index cache), or last-page-length metadata. Ask: support these as first-class MLA paging options.

**6. Expert-parallel dispatch contract (new; relates to MoE overhaul, project 45).**
All-to-all EP backends (e.g. MORI) use statically-sized dispatch buffers, per-local-expert token counts, and int32 top-k indices, and can't support some routing modes — differing from vLLM's more dynamic fused-MoE dispatch. Ask: generalize the dispatch contract to allow this metadata shape and a way to declare unsupported routing modes.

**Why this is materially different from the existing RFCs (per the contribution policy):**
#42082 standardizes *permutation-level* KV layout and connector code; #8913/#33314 decouple *linear* checkpoint formats from kernels. None of them currently expresses non-permutation physical layouts, MoE repacking, the extra quant axes, padding-as-shape, MLA page_size-1/aux caches, or the EP dispatch contract. This RFC is the union of those residual gaps, framed as extensions to land *within* the existing efforts where possible.

### Feedback Period.

~2 weeks.

### CC List.

(maintainers) @robertgshaw2-redhat @simon-mo @youkaichao @khluu
(KV) @LucasWilkinson @heheda12345 @NickLucche
(quant/linear) @mgoin @ProExpertProg @dsikka @bnellnm @BadrBasowid @tjtanaa
(AMD/ROCm) @dllehr-amd @Fangzhou-Ai @sunway513 @valarLip @wuhuikx @zejunchen-zejun

### Any Other Things.

Searched for relevant existing work before filing: #42082, #8913, #33314, #42449, #23161 and PRs #42374 / #44455 / #46992. We're happy to **split this per area** (e.g. fold the KV asks into #42082, the quant asks into #33314, and file padding / EP as separate small RFCs) if maintainers prefer that over one umbrella thread.

title: [RFC]: Streaming Derender for Disaggregated Serving
author: hickeyma
body:
### Motivation.

The batch derender endpoints (`/v1/chat/completions/derender`, `/v1/completions/derender`) landed in #43606 (detokenization) and #45919 (non-streaming reasoning/tool parsing). They consume `GenerateResponse` and emit a complete `ChatCompletionResponse`.

Many real world disaggregated consumers cannot use a batch only post processing tier:

- **Interactive serving** (llm-d, Dynamo) returns tokens to end clients as they are generated. Streaming is a **hard gating requirement** (ref: @bbrowning in https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/42729#issuecomment-4631310758).
- The producer side already streams e2e. `/inference/v1/generate` returns an SSE `StreamingResponse` when `request.stream` is set (`scale_out/token_in_token_out/api_router.py`), emitting `GenerateStreamResponse` chunks whose `GenerateResponseStreamChoice` carries the delta token IDs per step (`scale_out/token_in_token_out/serving.py`). `/render` already forwards `stream` / `stream_options`. **It therefore needs to be implemented on the  derender side.**

This RFC specifies a streaming derender that is the inverse of the streaming render path.

Partial:
- #34407
- #22817

Companion to:
- #42729

#### Why is this not a flag on the derender batch endpoint?

1. **Different input type.** The batch path (#42729) consumes a complete `GenerateResponse`. Streaming consumes `GenerateStreamResponse` *deltas*. It is therefore a distinct request shape and not a parameter on the existing endpoint.
2. **Incremental detokenization is stateful.** `IncrementalDetokenizer` carries `prefix_offset` / `read_offset` / prior tokens across `update()` calls. A naive per chunk `tokenizer.decode()` produces wrong spacing and can split multi-byte characters (see #44620). The per step delta `token_ids` are the right incremental input. `GenerateStreamResponse` however does **not** carry the detokenizer offsets and that state has to come from somewhere.
3. **Streaming parsers are stateful too.** Reasoning/tool parsers maintain incremental parse state across deltas (the reasoning to content/tool transition, partial tool call JSON). This compounds the state transport question below.

### Proposed Change.

#### New endpoints

| Method | Path | Input | Output |
|--------|------|-------|--------|
| `POST` | `/v1/chat/completions/derender` (`stream: true`) | `DerenderChatStreamRequest` | JSON `{ "chunk": ChatCompletionStreamResponse, "stream_state": DerenderStreamState }` |
| `POST` | `/v1/completions/derender` (`stream: true`) | `DerenderCompletionStreamRequest` | JSON `{ "chunk": CompletionStreamResponse, "stream_state": DerenderStreamState }` |

> [!NOTE]
> Streaming reuses the same `derender/` path with a `stream: true` flag, mirroring the producer (`/inference/v1/generate`). FastAPI validates a typed union discriminated on the `stream` literal and the handler dispatches with `isinstance`. The existing non-streaming types keep `generate_response` required.

Both endpoints run on the existing render server (GPU-free, only the `Renderer`/tokenizer) and are **stateless**.

#### Response format: plain JSON per call, not SSE

The derender is a **stateless per chunk translator**: one request in to one `{ "chunk", "stream_state" }` out. SSE out was rejected because it requires either a long lived connection or buffering all chunks before calling derender. This both conflict with the stateless design (Option A). The SSE protocol lives on the generate side and the final usage chunk are the client's responsibility.

#### Core design decision: incremental state (Option A, stateless)

The server returns updated state in each chunk. The client echoes it back on the next chunk. Server stays stateless and idempotent. There is no `request_id` keyed session and no lifecycle/eviction on the render tier.

Other design decision considered:

- **Option B (server-side session keyed by `request_id`)**: rejected because it breaks statelessness and adds session lifecycle + eviction + memory pressure.
- **Option C (shm state transport)**: deferred as a future optimization for large round tripped state on long generations. Only consider after Option A's payload cost is measured.

#### Parser state: replay (no opaque serialization)

Tool parsers hold internals we can't cheaply round trip (`prev_tool_call_arr`, `current_tool_id`, `streamed_args_for_tool`, engine lexer buffers). Rather than serialize them, the streaming chat derender **rebuilds a fresh parser each chunk by replaying the output tokens through it**, then feeds the new chunk and emits whatever the parser hands back.

Replay keeps the producer's chunk boundaries. `stream_state` carries `output_chunk_lens` (the token count of each chunk as it arrived) next to `output_token_ids`. Every chunk, replayed or live, goes through one `parse_delta` call. That matches standard serving which calls `parse_delta` once per engine step, so a multi-token step (e.g. speculative decoding) rebuilds the same parser state. Per token replay could diverge because some parser state (e.g. `history_tool_call_cnt`) advances once per `parse_delta` call. Text comes from a throwaway incremental detokenizer with `skip_special_tokens=False`, so the parser sees `</think>` / `<tool_call>` markers exactly as generate emits them.

Here are a few things to be aware of:

- **Cost:** transport is O(n) per chunk → O(n²) over a generation. Replay is one `parse_delta` call per prior chunk → O(n²) calls over a generation. `parse_delta` is itself O(n) for parsers that re-scan the accumulated text (Hermes tool call JSON, DeepSeek-R1 reasoning), so compute is O(n³) character work. `prompt_token_ids` is also sent and re-scanned on every chunk, so on long prompts it dominates the payload. Prompt + history + delta is bounded by `max_model_len` and rejected past it. Replay runs off the event loop on the renderer's executor (`renderer_num_workers`, default `1`), so size it for concurrent parser configured streams. Documented in `derenderer.md`.
- **Measured:** @shimib's benchmark (https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/56851#issuecomment-5685698033) found ~9× the in-process CPU at matched load and +15% E2E p50 on multi-thousand-token reasoning outputs. With the default single worker, the tier saturated under concurrent parsed streams.
- **Tool call ID stability:** IDs (`random_uuid()`, and `kimi_k2` style IDs derived from `history_tool_call_cnt`) are pinned in state and reused, so a replay never changes an ID the client has already seen. This isn't only defensive. Under `tool_choice="required"`, `extract_required_tool_call_streaming` resets `function_name_returned` to `False` whenever the partial JSON transiently fails to parse which makes a from scratch replay re-emit `id`+`name` for an index that already has one.
- **Future:** latency sensitive interactive traffic is better served by #56851, which keeps the parser alive for the request on the decode pool instead of replaying. For stateless consumers, an LRU of live `Parser` instances keyed by `(request_id, choice_index)` would skip replay on a cache hit and get compute back to O(delta) with no protocol change. It needs its own design for eviction, memory bounds and chunks routed to different replicas (#57571). Serializing parser state was tied to #32713 which was closed as not planned.

> [!NOTE]
> **This was originally specified as replay + diff** — re-run one-shot `parse()` over the accumulated output each chunk and diff against the last emission. Two reasons for the change in design:
>
> 1. `HarmonyParser.parse()` always calls `flush()` → `process_eos()`. Mid-stream that throws and the recovery path re-emits the in-flight message on the `final` channel. Partial reasoning comes out as content with a warning logged every chunk.
> 2. On partial markup like `<tool_call>{"name": "get_w`, `extract_tool_calls` fails the JSON load and returns the raw markup as content. Once the call completes, `parse()` returns *shorter* content and a diff that only moves forward can't take back what it already sent.
>
> `Parser.parse_delta()` and its `StreamState` landed after this RFC was written and gives the incremental semantics directly. So replay stays since it's still the answer to non-serializable parser state and the diff goes away. This swaps the diff step, not the replay step, so it isn't more expensive than what this RFC already accepted. The O(n³) above is the RFC's own replay cost stated more precisely.

#### Detokenization state: carried offsets

PR #47301 landed this differently than understood initially. Instead of rebuilding the decode window from the full token history each chunk, the state carries the incremental decode offsets directly: `prev_tokens` (the trailing window), `prefix_offset` and `read_offset`. `detokenize_incrementally` only ever reads `prev_tokens[prefix_offset:]`, so we carry just that tail then trim and rebase it after each chunk.

Compute is O(delta) per chunk and transport is O(window) which means the state doesn't grow with generation length. Held back multi-byte sequences still work because `read_offset` tracks the partially read character across the chunk boundary. Guarded by token-by-token CJK/emoji parity tests (`chunked == one-shot`) so #46159 stays fixed.

This only covers the completions path and the chat path with no parser. The parser path never reads these fields. It replays, carrying the output tokens instead (see above) and builds its own throwaway detok window per call. #46159 is guarded on that path too with
CJK/emoji tests across the reasoning→content transition.

#### Protocol additions

`vllm/entrypoints/scale_out/token_in_token_out/protocol.py`:

```python
class DerenderStreamState(BaseModel):
    # Detok state for completions, and chat with no parser. Bounded.
    prev_tokens: list[str] = []
    prefix_offset: int = Field(default=0, ge=0)
    read_offset: int = Field(default=0, ge=0)
    role_sent: bool = False               # emit role:"assistant" once
    # Parser path. Replay buffer, bounded by max_model_len.
    output_token_ids: list[int] = []
    output_chunk_lens: list[int] = []     # tokens per chunk, each > 0, sums to len(output_token_ids)
    tools_streamed: bool = False          # drives the finish_reason rewrite
    last_tool_call_ids: list[str] = []    # pinned IDs, stable across replays


class DerenderChatStreamRequest(BaseModel):
    stream: Literal[True]
    model: str | None = None
    generate_chunk: GenerateStreamResponse
    stream_state: DerenderStreamState | None = None  # absent on first chunk
    prompt_tokens: int | None = None                 # count, for usage
    prompt_token_ids: list[int] | None = None        # parser path
    chat_request: ChatCompletionRequest | None = None

class DerenderCompletionStreamRequest(BaseModel):
    stream: Literal[True]
    model: str | None = None
    generate_chunk: GenerateStreamResponse
    stream_state: DerenderStreamState | None = None
    prompt_tokens: int | None = None
    completion_request: CompletionRequest | None = None
```

The existing non-streaming types gain `stream: Literal[False] = False` (backward compatible).

`last_content` / `last_reasoning` from #47301 are removed as they are not required.

`prompt_token_ids` is added. `parse_delta` needs the prompt IDs to work out whether reasoning is already open when generation starts. Chat templates that end in `<think>` misclassify the first tokens without it. The existing `prompt_tokens` is a usage count and can't stand in. Clients already have the IDs: they come back as `GenerateRequest.token_ids` from `/render`. It stays optional on the model (a caller with no parser configured never sends it) and is enforced server side instead.

`output_chunk_lens` is added so replay can reuse the chunk boundaries the generate stream produced (see Parser state). It grows by one entry per chunk which is one per token without speculative decoding.

Responses are typed too: `DerenderChatStreamResponse` and `DerenderCompletionStreamResponse`, each `{chunk, stream_state}`.

**On state size.** The replay buffer is O(n) and there's no way around that. Rebuilding parser state without serializing it is what replay means. It's bounded by `max_model_len` and rejected past that. Everything else (completions, chat without a parser) keeps the bounded window and pays nothing.

> [!NOTE]
> **Single delta, not a list.** The batch `DerenderCompletionRequest` carries `list[GenerateResponse]`. Streaming is inherently per stream, so each chunk carries one `generate_chunk`. Fan out over multiple completions becomes N independent streams with one `DerenderStreamState` each (keyed by `choice.index`) and not a batched list. The completions path leaves the parser fields (output_token_ids, output_chunk_lens, tools_streamed, last_tool_call_ids) unused.

##### Message validation

`stream_state` is entirely client controlled, so the streaming chat endpoint validates before it touches the tokenizer and returns `400` and never `500`:

- **`chat_request` missing while a parser is configured** → reject. Falling through to plain detok would leak raw harmony/tool markup into `content`. The same check now applies to the **batch** path which silently degraded this way before PR #50550 (same class of bug as #45834).
- **`prompt_token_ids` missing while a parser is configured** → reject, rather than silently misclassifying prompt opened reasoning as content.
- **More than one choice in a chunk** → reject. One `DerenderStreamState` is threaded through the chunk, so multiple choices would corrupt each other's detok/parser state.
- **`len(prompt_token_ids) + len(output_token_ids) + len(delta)` over `max_model_len`** → reject. This bounds the replay buffer and the prompt re-scan every chunk does.
- **Inconsistent `output_chunk_lens`** (doesn't sum to `len(output_token_ids)`, or contains a zero entry) → rejected when the request is validated.

An unexpected parser failure on well typed but malformed state also surfaces as a `400` rather than an unhandled `500`: Hermes swallows its own streaming exceptions but `finalize_generation` and the engine based parsers do not.

#### Streaming flow

```
client                         render tier (stateless)
  │  DerenderChatStreamRequest(generate_chunk Δ_0, stream_state=None)
  ├──────────────────────────────►  fresh parser, feed Δ_0 through parse_delta
  │  { chunk: Δ_0, stream_state: S_0 }
  ◄──────────────────────────────┤
  │  DerenderChatStreamRequest(generate_chunk Δ_1, stream_state=S_0)
  ├──────────────────────────────►  fresh parser, replay S_0 history one
  │                                 parse_delta per original chunk (discarded),
  │                                 then feed Δ_1 in one call
  ◄──────────────────────────────┤
  │              ...
  │  final usage chunk (client driven)
```

#### Streaming parsers

Parsers are driven through `parse_delta()`, one call per chunk as it arrived from generate, on a parser rebuilt from replay. It is not through one-shot `parse()` over an accumulated window. Token based parsers (Harmony `openai_tool_parser`, `is_reasoning_end` boundary logic) work unchanged since `parse_delta` receives both the decoded text and the token IDs for each step. Decoding uses `skip_special_tokens=False` so markers reach the parser intact.

`parse_delta` also needs the **prompt** token IDs to settle whether reasoning is already open when generation starts which is why `prompt_token_ids` is new on the request (see Protocol additions). The U+FFFD reasoning to content/tool transition fix (#46159) must not regress and is covered by chunk boundary tests on the parser path.

#### PR breakdown

- **PR1 detok only streaming derender** (#47301, **merged**): carried offset detok state, protocol types, both stream methods (chat parser path stubbed), typed request and response models on the shared paths, unit + integration tests.
- **PR2 chat streaming derender (replay)** (#50550, **merged**): real parse path. Replays output tokens through `parse_delta` on a fresh parser, keeping the original chunk boundaries (`output_chunk_lens`). Emits reasoning/content/tool_call deltas, pins tool call IDs, rewrites `finish_reason` to `tool_calls` and filters parallel tool calls. Adds `prompt_token_ids` and the fail closed 400s above (including on the batch path).  Passes `model_config` to the batch parser (batch derender still discards the parser's tool call IDs, tracked under #42729). Does not regress #46159. Documents the O(n³).
- **PR3 parity CI + docs** (**merged**): extend `render → generate → derender → render == render` parity to the chunked path. Document the protocol, the Option A state model, the client loop contract and the `stream: true` symmetry with `/inference/v1/generate`.

Also needed to close this RFC:

- **Streaming logprobs:** #55029 for the plain path, then the parsed path. **[Merged]**
- **Plain path on the renderer executor:** #57528 (fixes #57350). **[Merged]**

Deferred, tracked separately:

- Parser cache / server side parser state, including tool call ID stability across retried calls (#57571).
- Shared per choice `ChatStreamProcessor` for chat serving and derender (#57572). **[Merged]**

### Feedback Period.

No response

### CC List.

@DarkLight1337 @noooop @hyeongyun0916 @vMaroon @sagearc @robertgshaw2-redhat @njhill @aoshen02 @bbrowning @NickLucche

### Any Other Things.

#### Out of scope

- gRPC / msgpack transport (JSON/pydantic first, per #22817).
- Torch free / in-process parser library (#38925): orthogonal.
- `token_id:N` logprob shape redesign: tracked separately (#57574). Streaming logprobs themselves are in scope (see PR breakdown).
- Serialized parser state: dropped. #32713 was closed as not planned. Replay cost is handled by #56851 for latency sensitive P/D and optionally by a parser cache (#57571) for stateless consumers.  

#### Resolved questions

- **`parser_state` serialization:** avoided by replaying tokens through `parse_delta` on a fresh parser each chunk. #32713 was closed as not planned.
- **State transport:** **Option A** (stateless, client carried). B rejected. **C (shm) deferred.**
- **Routing:** same path + `stream: true`. FastAPI validates a typed union on the `stream` literal and the handler picks with `isinstance`. No manual JSON peeking.
- **Response format:** plain JSON per call. SSE out rejected as incompatible with Option A.
- **Parser path when the caller omits `chat_request` / `prompt_token_ids`:** fail closed with a 400 and is not a documented degradation. Both are recoverable client side. Silently emitting markup or misfiled reasoning is not.
- **Replay granularity:** one `parse_delta` call per original chunk, recovered from `output_chunk_lens`. Not one per token.
- **Replay cost:** measured (https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/56851#issuecomment-5685698033). Latency sensitive P/D goes to #56851 rather than adding server side state to the render tier.

#### Related

- #42729 (batch derender RFC, parent of this RFC)
- #34407
- #22817
- #32713
- #36166
- #38925
- #44620
- #46159
- #50550 (PR2)

- #57350 / #57528 (plain streaming path on the event loop)
- #47931 (batch `finish_reason` for tool calls)

title: [RFC]: Port vLLM-built Hopper and Blackwell C++ CUDA kernels to CuTeDSL
author: LucasWilkinson
body:
## Summary

Port all vLLM-built Hopper and Blackwell CUDA C++ kernels from in-tree C++/CUTLASS implementations to CuTeDSL where feasible.

The goal is a build-free development install for common Hopper and Blackwell environments: contributors should be able to install vLLM and iterate on kernels without local vLLM CUDA C++ builds.

This builds on the motivation from [#17419 Kernel Library Restructure / Packaging Split](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/17419): vLLM source builds are too slow, and most development does not require rebuilding `csrc`.

## Motivation

vLLM source builds are expensive, largely because of custom CUDA/C++ kernels. This slows down local setup, ordinary development, kernel experiments, and CI/debug cycles.

The problem is growing for Hopper and Blackwell as vLLM adds more SM90, SM100, SM103, SM120, and SM121-specific kernels. CuTeDSL gives us a path to keep optimized architecture-specific kernels while reducing the amount of CUDA/C++ code built directly by vLLM.

## Build Timing Data

Measured on commit `40e5522121` (`main`, 2026-06-23) on an 8x H200 host with CUDA 13.0, PyTorch 2.11.0+cu130, Ninja 1.13.0, and `MAX_JOBS=160`.

`uv pip install -e . --torch-backend=auto` took 930s wall clock. A cold-cache (no ccache/sccache), took 747s wall clock.

Ninja recorded 392 timed build steps over 727s wall clock. CUDA object compilation accounted for 369 steps and 55,383s of summed compile time across parallel jobs.

| Area | Build steps | Summed compile time | Slowest file |
| --- | ---: | ---: | --- |
| vllm-flash-attn FA3 | 194 | 32,740s | 299s, `flash_fwd_hdim128_bf16_softcap_packgqa_sm90.cu.o` |
| vllm-flash-attn FA2 | 55 | 11,736s | 425s, `flash_fwd_split_hdim64_fp16_sm80.cu.o` |
| Core `_C_stable_libtorch` | 78 | 7,466s | 724s, `scaled_mm_c2x.cu.o` |
| MoE `_moe_C_stable_libtorch` | 26 | 2,497s | 237s, `sm80_kernel_bfloat16_u8b128_bfloat16.cu.o` |
| FlashMLA | 27 | 1,321s | 175s, `fmha_cutlass_fwd_sm100.cu.o` |

Top slowest files in `_C_stable_libtorch`:

| File | Compile time |
| --- | ---: |
| `csrc/libtorch_stable/quantization/w8a8/cutlass/scaled_mm_c2x.cu` | 724s |
| `csrc/libtorch_stable/attention/paged_attention_v2.cu` | 334s |
| `csrc/libtorch_stable/attention/paged_attention_v1.cu` | 328s |

## Proposal

Port all vLLM-built Hopper and Blackwell CUDA kernels to CuTeDSL where technically feasible. The target end state is that Hopper/Blackwell development installs do not require local vLLM CUDA C++ builds and raw CUDA performance remains competitive.

## Scope

This RFC covers Hopper and Blackwell kernels built by vLLM. The main targets are quantized GEMMs, MoE kernels, sparse/compressor kernels, and attention-adjacent kernels where CuTeDSL or FA4 is the expected long-term path.

The warmup/cache/JIT-monitoring infrastructure needed to avoid JIT compilation during serving and the resulting ITL spikes will be discussed in a subsequent RFC.

This RFC does not propose porting Ampere kernels to CuTeDSL. It also does not propose rewriting kernels without performance validation or investing in FA3-specific CuTeDSL work expected to be superseded by FA4.

For Hopper attention, the expected direction is to replace FA3 with FA4 once FA4 decode performance is sufficiently optimized. CuTeDSL work should target the forward-looking FA4 path rather than duplicating long-term effort on FA3.

## Active / Previous Work

CuTeDSL kernel work:

- [#43584 Add CuTe DSL sparse compressor support](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/43584)
- [#44230 Optimize the compressor 128 split CuTeDSL kernel](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/44230)
- [#44501 Quant scaled-mm FP8/INT8 kernel in CuTeDSL](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/44501)
- [#42899 Add CuTeDSL DSV4 indexer FP8 kernel](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/42899)
- [#42562 Add CuTeDSL generic LL BF16 router GEMM](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/42562)
- [#44343 Add CuTeDSL generic LL FP32 router GEMM](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/44343)

CuTeDSL operational work:

- [#46167 Runtime monitor for post-warmup CuTeDSL compilation](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/46167)
- [#46182 CuTeDSL warmup infrastructure, FA4 MLA](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/46182)
- [#45270 CuTeDSL JIT warmup/cache init PoC](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/45270)

## Benchmarking Requirements

Each port should report raw CUDA kernel time and end-to-end serving impact, cold-JIT and warmed behavior, and Hopper and Blackwell results separately.

## Success Criteria

This effort is successful if common Hopper/Blackwell development installs do not require local vLLM CUDA C++ builds and wheel build time is meaningfully reduced. Raw CUDA performance should be competitive with existing native kernels, end-to-end serving performance should not regress, and runtime JIT should not occur during serving.

## Risks

### Startup Time Increase

CuTeDSL can move cost from install time to runtime, so startup time may increase. We should keep warmups close to what the deployment will require at runtime. We may also want to look at producing JIT caches ahead-of-time.

title: [RFC]: Sparse-attention-based self-speculative decoding (StreamingLLM, then Vegas)
author: npz7yyk
body:
### Motivation.

Long-context decoding is typically bottlenecked by the KV cache access. Self-speculative decoding with sparse attention [1] drafts tokens using the target model over a subset of the KV cache, then verifies them in parallel against the full cache. This delivers a lossless speedup with no separate draft model, no extra weights, and no training.

vLLM's spec-decode framework currently covers ngram, Eagle, Medusa, and MTP. These proposers either require a draft model or rely on n-gram matching. None supports a same-model, sparse-KV draft. This RFC adds one.

I am a co-author of Vegas [2]. While developing Vegas, I implemented self-speculative decoding with sparse attention in vLLM, with two sparse attention algorithms for drafting: StreamingLLM (sliding window with attention sink) [3] and Vegas. Measured as accumulated decoding throughput on one H100 with Qwen3-8B, replaying AIME 2025 [4] prompts 32 times: vanilla vLLM reaches ~1,000 tokens/s; the StreamingLLM drafter (`num_speculative_tokens=4`) reaches ~1,600 tokens/s; Vegas (`num_speculative_tokens=6`) reaches ~1,850 tokens/s. More evaluation results are available in the Vegas [paper](https://arxiv.org/abs/2602.07223).

A runnable implementation built on vLLM v0.16.0 with benchmark is public at https://github.com/platformxlab/vegas ([feature commit](https://github.com/platformxlab/vegas/commit/f49fd737a22c2e36a461600e85cc24f6177c27af)). I'd like to upstream it in two PRs.

[1] MagicDec: Breaking the Latency-Throughput Tradeoff for Long Context Generation with Speculative Decoding [arxiv:2408.11049](https://arxiv.org/abs/2408.11049)  
[2] Vegas: Self-Speculative Decoding with Verification-Guided Sparse Attention [arXiv:2602.07223](https://arxiv.org/abs/2602.07223)  
[3] Efficient Long-Context Generation with Sliding Window and Attention Sink [arXiv:2309.17453](https://arxiv.org/abs/2309.17453)  
[4] American Invitational Mathematics Examination (AIME) 2025 [`math-ai/aime25`](https://huggingface.co/datasets/math-ai/aime25)

### Proposed Change.

Add a new speculative method `method="sparse_attn"` with a `SparseAttnProposer` that reuses the target model to draft under a sparse KV pattern, selected by a `sparse_attn_algorithm` knob.

- **PR 1:** the proposer framework + **StreamingLLM** as the default sparse pattern. A runnable branch is available at [`npz7yyk/vegas@vllm-pr1`](https://github.com/npz7yyk/vegas/tree/vllm-pr1), based on vLLM [`releases/v0.24.0`](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/tree/releases/v0.24.0) (commit [`ee0da84ab`](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/commit/ee0da84ab)), and it forward-ports cleanly to `main`; a PR is thus ready to be submitted once the approach is confirmed here.
- **PR 2:** **Vegas** algorithm (verification-guided KV selection). This needs a small flash-attention change to expose per-token attention logits from the verify pass as a byproduct; I'll propose that separately against the FA repo.

New config fields on `SpeculativeConfig`:

| Field | Meaning | Default |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `sparse_attn_algorithm` | sparse KV pattern (`"streamingllm"`) | `"streamingllm"` |
| `sparse_attn_ratio` | fraction of KV kept for drafting | `0.05` |
| `sparse_attn_min_tokens` | floor on per-request KV budget | `256` |

### PR 1: framework + StreamingLLM

New self-contained module:

```text
vllm/v1/spec_decode/sparse_attn/
├── __init__.py                     # exports SparseAttnProposer
├── proposer.py                     # SparseAttnProposer: drives the self-speculative draft loop
└── attn_overrider/
    ├── __init__.py                 # BaseAttnOverrider + build_attention_overrider() dispatch
    └── streamingllm.py             # StreamingLLMAttnOverrider: sink + sliding-window pattern
```

Wiring into existing vLLM files:

| File | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| `vllm/config/speculative.py` | Adds `method="sparse_attn"` + the `sparse_attn_*` fields |
| `vllm/v1/worker/gpu_model_runner.py` | Constructs and drives `SparseAttnProposer` |
| `vllm/v1/core/sched/scheduler.py` | Reserves lookahead slots so KV pages are allocated for draft tokens |

The change is a self-contained new module plus small, localized wiring edits (config + scheduler lookahead + model-runner dispatch); it does not touch the existing spec-decode proposers.

### PR 2: Vegas

Adds one algorithm slot + its kernels, and swaps in the flash-attention build that exposes per-token attention scores:

```text
vllm/v1/spec_decode/sparse_attn/attn_overrider/
├── vegas.py                        # VegasAttnOverrider: verification-guided KV selection
└── utils/
    ├── __init__.py
    ├── varlen_reduce.py            # CUDA kernel: reduce per-query scores -> per-token metric
    └── varlen_topk.py              # CUDA kernel: variable-length top-k KV selection
```

Plus small edits:

| File | Change |
| --- | --- |
| `attn_overrider/__init__.py` | Register the `"vegas"` branch in the dispatch |
| `vllm/config/speculative.py` | Add `"vegas"` to the `sparse_attn_algorithm` choices |
| companion flash-attention PR | Expose per-token logits via a `scores` output on `flash_attn_varlen_func` (separate PR against the FA repo) |

### Potential Concern

To keep `SparseAttnProposer` self-contained, the sparse KV pattern is currently applied by wrapping the attention backend at runtime during the draft pass (FlashAttention for now). It works, but a runtime wrap of core attention is a design choice I'd like input on: is this acceptable, or would maintainers prefer a more formal override mechanism in the attention layer? Happy to align with whatever fits vLLM's attention abstraction best.

title: [RFC]: ReplaySSM: cache SSM inputs instead of state for faster standard and speculative decode (Mamba2 + GDN)
author: Johnny-Liou
body:
### Motivation.

## Summary

[ReplaySSM](https://dao-lab.ai/blog/2026/replayssm/) is a memory-bandwidth optimization for the decode kernels of state space model (SSM) and linear attention layers. It is a collaboration between Dao AI Lab and NVIDIA; a concurrent cross-framework implementation is in the [TensorRT-LLM PR](https://github.com/NVIDIA/TensorRT-LLM/pull/14203).

SSM decode is memory-bound: today each step reads and writes back the full recurrent state. ReplaySSM instead caches recent inputs, reconstructing the state only when needed and otherwise computing the output directly from the cache. This keeps most steps read-only and writes the full state back only once every L steps. 

ReplaySSM provides three benefits:

1. Memory-traffic reduction in a bandwidth-bound kernel: the per-step state write is replaced by a small input append.
2. Cheap rollback for speculative decoding: caching recent SSM inputs makes rollback a buffer pointer move, avoiding the separate per-draft-token state the current implementation keeps.
3. Parallel verification for speculative decoding: on non-flush steps the output is read directly without materializing the state, so a draft window is verified in one shot instead of by a serial recurrence.

Implementation: we have opened a draft PR (#47576) implementing ReplaySSM in vLLM, based on the [ReplaySSM reference repository](https://github.com/Johnny-Liou/ReplaySSM). 

We are aware of the existing feature request #46187, which tracks ReplaySSM in vLLM and is assigned to us as the ReplaySSM authors. This RFC and the accompanying draft PR are the upstream contribution we committed to.

## Motivation

Two problems motivate ReplaySSM.

1. In hybrid models, the SSM (linear-attention) layers are the decode bottleneck at short-to-medium output lengths (Fig 2 in the blog post). SSM decode is memory-bound and its per-step state read/write dominates HBM traffic.
2. Speculative decoding must roll back rejected draft tokens, but the SSM state update is irreversible: once history is summarized into the recurrent state, a token cannot be subtracted back out. To support rollback, the current implementation keeps a separate recurrent state per draft token, which costs extra memory traffic and extra HBM footprint (about (1 + num_spec)× the state), hurting both latency and maximum concurrency.

ReplaySSM addresses both by caching inputs instead of state. It keeps a single checkpoint state S0 and caches the recent SSM inputs in a ring buffer; on a flush step (once every L steps) it folds the cached inputs into the checkpoint, and on every other step it computes the output directly from the checkpoint plus the cached inputs without materializing the full state.

For standard decode, writing the state back only once every L steps (instead of every step) roughly halves the dominant memory traffic. For speculative decode, caching recent inputs makes rollback a ring-buffer pointer move, cutting the per-step rollback cost from O(T) to O(1) (`T = num_spec_tokens + 1`) and removing the per-draft-token state storage, which improves both latency and maximum concurrency.

ReplaySSM speeds up the SSM kernel most at large serving batch sizes, where the kernel is fully memory-bound (small batch is not a relevant operating point: there the kernel is overhead-bound rather than memory-bound, and e2e latency is dominated by the MLP layers). For hybrid models it gives the largest end-to-end speedup at short-to-medium output lengths, where the SSM layers dominate latency.

### Proposed Change.

## Proposed Change

We propose adding ReplaySSM to vLLM as an opt-in decode path for hybrid SSM models, covering both SSM families and both decode modes, with the baseline path unchanged when the feature is off.

### Scope
- Mamba2 and Gated DeltaNet (GDN) SSM layers.
- Standard and speculative decode.
- New Triton kernels plus the vLLM integration (mixer dispatch, attention-metadata cursors, state-shape sizing). The conv path reuses vLLM's existing `causal_conv1d_update` unchanged.

### Integration and backward compatibility
The feature is opt-in through config flags that all default to off; when off, the decode path is byte-for-byte the baseline. The ReplaySSM caches are added as extra tensors on the existing paged mamba state, so they reuse vLLM's paged-block allocation and block-table indexing (continuous batching, per-request allocation and eviction).

### Config flags (all default off)
- `--use-replayssm`: Mamba2/GDN standard cached decode.
- `--use-replayssm-spec`: speculative cached decode (requires speculative decoding and `--mamba-cache-mode none`).
- `--replayssm-buffer-len`: history buffer length (default 16).
- `--replayssm-route` (Mamba2 standard only): `output_only` (default) or `state_and_output`; a temporary knob for the precision study, planned for removal (see Open questions).

### Key integration points
- Paged cache: the input caches and the checkpoint state live in the paged KV block, indexed per request by physical block id; only small per-block cursors live in the metadata builder.
- CUDA graphs and continuous batching: speculative decode uses two device-routed launches (verify and flush) with the flush decision and rollback computed on-device, so the launch sequence is fixed and one captured graph per batch size covers the path.
- What we cache: only the state-building inputs; the output read vector (Mamba2 C, GDN q) is taken from the current activations and never cached.
- Flush decision (spec): we flush when `history + T > B`, where `B` is the history buffer length, and size the ring buffer to `B + T`. This is a slight change from the formulation in the blog post.

### Validation
Correctness is checked at three levels (per-kernel vs an exact reference, prefill-vs-decode equivalence over full sequences, and engine-level parity via `check_logprobs_close`), plus a speculative-decode acceptance-length match on GSM8K. Performance covers standard decode (kernel and end-to-end) and speculative decode (throughput and maximum concurrency). Full numbers are in the draft PR.

## Performance
Please check the detailed experiment results in the draft PR (#47576). Here are brief results.

### Standard decode
Whole-model per-step speedup (baseline / ReplaySSM), fp32 state, buffer length 16:

| Model (SSM, HW) | bs 1 | bs 32 | bs 128 | bs 512 |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Nemotron-Nano-4B (Mamba2, H100) | 0.99 | 1.17 | 1.40 | 1.55 |
| Qwen3.5-4B (GDN, H100) | 0.99 | 1.08 | 1.21 | 1.31 |
| Nemotron-Super-120B (Mamba2, B300) | 0.98 | 1.10 | 1.27 | 1.67 |
| Qwen3.5-122B (GDN, B300) | 0.98 | 1.07 | 1.14 | 1.20 |

### Speculative decode
End-to-end throughput at (B, T) = (16, 4), on B300 with an MTP drafter. `c/std` = ReplaySSM-spec / baseline-spec throughput; `c/AR` = ReplaySSM-spec / no-spec autoregressive throughput.

ReplaySSM-spec vs native-spec (`c/std`):

| Model | bs 1 | bs 32 | bs 256 |
|---|---|---|---|
| Nemotron-Super-120B (Mamba2) | 1.09 | 1.07 | 1.88 |
| Qwen3.5-122B (GDN) | 0.99 | 1.19 | 1.80 |

ReplaySSM-spec vs no-spec AR (`c/AR`):

| Model | bs 1 | bs 32 | bs 256 |
|---|---|---|---|
| Nemotron-Super-120B (Mamba2) | 2.12 | 1.90 | 2.21 |
| Qwen3.5-122B (GDN) | 1.90 | 1.93 | 1.85 |

### Feedback Period.

## Feedback Period
One week from posting; we will keep it open longer if discussion is active.

### CC List.

_No response_

### Any Other Things.

## Work in progress
1. Tensor parallelism test files (e.g., TP1==TP2) and evaluation.
2. Evaluation on lower-precision (fp16/fp8) state. Current evaluation focus on FP32 state (default in most hybrid models)
3. Numerical-precision benefit: because reconstruction is FP32 and the state is written back only on flushes, a low-precision checkpoint (e.g. FP16) is re-quantized ~`L`× less often than the per-step baseline. Reference: [NVIDIA Nemotron-3-Ultra Technical Report](https://research.nvidia.com/labs/nemotron/files/NVIDIA-Nemotron-3-Ultra-Technical-Report.pdf), Section 4.5.

## Open questions
1. Timeline: We plan to split the integration into three stages: Mamba2 standard decode -> GDN standard decode -> Mamba2/GDN speculative decode. 
2. Paged-cache layout: is appending ReplaySSM tensors onto the mamba state the pattern you prefer, or should the caches be a separate allocation?
